About the role
We already run two kinds of agent alongside our teams. AI agents diagnose performance problems and tell people the root cause. Rule-based agents recommend marketing actions to our advertising teams. The quality of their decisions shows up directly in our revenue.
Next, both take a greater role in the day-to-day running of our lead generation business, moving from recommending, to acting with a person's approval, to acting on their own where it is safe. We need an engineer to build agents that are dependable in production, measurable, and safe to trust with more.
This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll own agents end to end, from understanding the workflow to running them in production, alongside our existing AI engineer, data scientists, product managers and the people who use the agents every day. Today we use Claude and open-weight models such as GLM, chosen per task on quality and cost, on an agent framework we build ourselves.

What you'll do
Build agents

- Start from the workflow. Sit with the operators, map how the work is actually done, and build for that, not for the process as documented.

- Build on shared rules. Rule-based and LLM agents that call shared, versioned rules and tools, not logic hard-coded inside each agent.

- Connect them to the business. Using our data warehouse, internal services, and the APIs into the systems agents act in.

- Turn outputs into results people trust. Structured outputs, validation and clear application logic.

Make them safe to trust

- Log every decision. Each action records its context, what was chosen, and whether a person accepted or overrode it, so agents can be evaluated and improved.

- Build the path to autonomy. Per decision, agents move from recommend, to act with approval, to act alone. Our data scientists propose the bar from agreement and override data and point people in the business sign it off; you build the mechanism that enforces it on our shared agent framework, with permissions and guardrails in the code, not the prompt.

- Evaluate behaviour, not just code. Test sets, agreement with expert operators, and evaluation before and after every change.

- Run what you ship. Tracing, failure handling, and tracking quality, latency and cost. There's no on-call rota.

What we're offering you:

- Family Forward support for our MVF parents and their mini-mes

- 2 charity days a year

What we're looking for

- 3+ years of engineering, including at least one LLM application or agent shipped to real users.

- Python and TypeScript: production-grade in one and productive in the other, with typed, tested code and clear interfaces. You'll work in both here.

- LLM engineering: tool calling, structured outputs, context management, and evaluating agent behaviour on representative test sets.

- Integration and operations: SQL, HTTP APIs, containers, CI/CD and a cloud platform, and debugging from logs and traces.

Nice to have

- Agents used daily by operators, with a feedback loop.

- AWS SageMaker, AWS ECS/Fargate, Terraform and CircleCI.

- Snowflake and dbt.

- Event logging for analytics or machine learning.

- Lead generation or ad tech.

How you'll work

- Commercial impact. You understand how the business creates value and use that to make better choices about what gets built, prioritised or stopped. You define the intended impact before starting, consider the cost of the work and evaluate what happened afterwards.

- Delivery and ownership. You take responsibility for outcomes and move at a pace matched to the cost of delay. You follow work through until it is delivered, handed over or deliberately stopped, and remain accountable for what happens after delivery.

- Candour and communication. You surface important information early, including when it is uncomfortable, with evidence and a view on what to do about it. You communicate what is known, assumed and uncertain in a form the audience can understand and act on.

- Making others better. You create lasting improvement in other people's and the team's work through teaching, feedback or challenge, and take challenge on your own work as readily as you give it.

- Growth and mastery. You deepen your capability through deliberate practice, feedback and experience, build the skills the work will need next, and change established practices when better approaches become available.

- Judgement under ambiguity. You make sound decisions with incomplete information and know when to act, escalate or delegate. You own what you ship regardless of how it was produced, and change position when the evidence changes.

How you'll build

- Craft and AI-native delivery. You build robust agents and AI applications, choosing the right approach for the problem, including when deterministic code is enough. You understand and can explain the evidence, assumptions, behaviour and limitations of what you build, and use AI to increase delivery speed without giving up technical ownership.

You design reliable systems that move agents and AI capabilities from a business problem into effective use, deciding what should be probabilistic and what deterministic. You treat data and context, security and governance, monitoring and observability, failure handling and recovery, cost, performance and lifecycle as part of the design rather than concerns added afterwards.

Machine Learning Engineer

Location: London

Salary: £95,000-120,000

Contract: Permanent

Working pattern: On site, 3 days a week

A new software venture built inside an established global provider of analytical and research services to the private capital industry is hiring Machine Learning Engineers to build the models, agents and evaluation systems that investment professionals rely on to analyse data, work with documents and automate research. You'll join the UK core team of around thirty people, working in Python on production ML and LLM systems that sit behind data-dense enterprise products.

THE ROLE

You'll report to the Head of Engineering and own the machine learning layer of the platform, from the first prototype through to a monitored production service. The work combines applied LLM engineering with the rigour that high-stakes financial workflows demand.

- The hard part is reliability and measurement: a model that is right most of the time is not enough when analysts act on the output, so every system needs to be evaluated, observable and safe to fail.

- Part of an engineering cohort being hired across machine learning, front-end and back-end.

- Based with the UK core team of around thirty people in Kings Cross, alongside colleagues in London and India.

WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Your remit spans the models and agents, the data and retrieval layer, the evaluation framework and the production platform.

- Design, build and ship LLM-powered features and multi-step agent workflows in Python, from prototype to production.

- Build document intelligence pipelines that extract, structure and reason over long, messy financial documents such as filings, decks, models and data rooms.

- Develop retrieval-augmented generation systems, including chunking, embeddings, vector search, re-ranking and citation, so that every answer can be traced to its source.

- Create evaluation frameworks and datasets, with automated regression tests, human review loops and metrics for accuracy, that catch mistakes early and stop the same failures recurring.

- Implement guardrails, confidence signalling and safe failure behaviour, and work with front-end colleagues to expose approvals, tool calls and partial progress to users.

- Fine-tune, prompt-engineer and benchmark models, and make considered decisions between hosted foundation models, open-weight models and classical ML on cost, latency and quality.

- Build and operate ML services and APIs with authentication, role-based access and tenant isolation, so client data is never mixed across tenants.

- Own MLOps in production: experiment tracking, model and prompt versioning, monitoring, drift detection, cost and latency management, and incident response.

- Write unit, integration and evaluation tests, and ship through Jenkins and SonarQube pipelines to AWS.

- Work with back-end and front-end engineers and with domain experts in private capital to turn real analyst workflows into reliable products.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- 5+ years in machine learning or software engineering, with production ML experience and strong Python.

- Hands-on experience shipping LLM-based or NLP systems to real users, including RAG, agents and tool use, and the ability to explain the design and trade-off decisions behind them.

- A rigorous approach to evaluation: you can define what "good" means for a model, build the test set and measure it.

- Strong grounding in the ML stack, such as PyTorch, scikit-learn, Hugging Face and vector databases, alongside sound software engineering practice.

- Experience deploying and monitoring models on cloud infrastructure, ideally AWS, with Git, CI/CD and containerisation.

- Experience building SaaS or multi-tenant products, with a working understanding of data security, access control and privacy.

- Daily use of AI coding tools such as Cursor or Claude Code, and a considered view of where they help.

- A degree in computer science, engineering, mathematics, statistics or a related field, or equivalent experience. A postgraduate degree is valued but not required.

NICE TO HAVE

- Experience building agentic products, including orchestration, memory, tool calling and human-in-the-loop controls.

- Document understanding, OCR and table extraction on complex financial documents.

- Fine-tuning or distillation of language models, and inference optimisation.

- Experience with financial, investment or other regulated-industry data.

- Experience with LLM observability and evaluation tooling.

THE REALITY

- Autonomous systems are being built inside high-stakes live businesses, where decisions carry real consequences and waiting for everyone to agree is not always an option.

- The systems will sometimes get things wrong; in this phase the London team needs to create the evaluations, visibilities and safeguards that catch mistakes early and stop the same failures recurring.

- The goal is to build the foundations of an enterprise-grade technology platform serving a multi-billion dollar serviceable market, and to share in that growth.

IN OUR CONVERSATIONS

Come ready to discuss three pieces of work:

- A production ML or LLM system you shipped: the architecture, data and cost decisions.

- An evaluation approach you designed to measure or improve quality, and what it revealed.

- A failure or regression you found in production and the improvement you made to prevent it recurring.

LOCATION & WORKING PATTERN

- Kings Cross, London. In office 3 days a week.

- Colleagues based in London and India.

- Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

- The interview process is intended to complete within three weeks, and adjustments to interviews can be arranged on request.

Position Summary
GSK's Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. You will lead the Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) function — the front of the Enterprise AI delivery pipeline that proves AI ideas with the business through PoCs, PoVs, MVPs and, where appropriate, first production versions, before handing proven solutions off to the Solutions Engineer for scale-up. This pattern is proven by AI-native companies such as Anthropic, Palantir and OpenAI, and this role brings that model to GSK.

You will hold direct line management of the FDE team (Staff, Lead, Senior, and Forward Deployed Engineers), setting FDE strategy and engagement priorities, owning Director-level BU sponsor relationships, and representing Enterprise AI on FDE matters to GSK leadership — while continuing to contribute technically at the frontier of AI-augmented engineering, where humans steer and agents execute. Enterprise AI's credibility with the business depends on engineers who can land inside BU problems, prove value quickly, and hand off cleanly; you will build and lead the function that makes this happen.

Responsibilities
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

- Lead the Forward Deployed Engineering function — strategy, structure, hiring, development, and standards for the function.

- Hire, mentor, and develop the FDE team — creating development paths from G8 through to G5.

- Set the standards for AI-native engineering practice within the function — agent workflows, prompt and pattern libraries, handoff hygiene.

- Own relationships with Director and Senior Director-level BU sponsors across business units that bring AI use cases to Enterprise AI.

- Take on the most strategic FDE engagements personally — the ones that set precedents for the function.

- Make and defend portfolio-level kill/continue decisions across FDE engagements with BU and Enterprise AI leadership.

- Coordinate with the Solutions Engineering and Operations Engineering functions on the delivery pipeline; represent FDE in Enterprise AI leadership forums.

- Influence vendor strategy and tooling choices for AI-native engineering practice within Enterprise AI.

- Ensure the FDE function operates within Code Orange, Responsible AI, and Accountability Report governance from the prototype stage onward.

- Provide regular reporting to Enterprise AI leadership on FDE function performance — engagement pipeline, outcomes, team development, and capacity.

Why You?
Basic Qualification
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals

- PhD or master’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- 12 or more years of experience in software engineering and AI/ML engineering, with significant time leading senior engineering teams or functions.

- Demonstrated experience taking AI ideas from sketch to working software at speed, in customer-facing engineering roles.

- Strong technical depth in GenAI patterns: agents, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, and evaluation.

- Daily use of AI coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Databricks AI Assistant) as the primary mode of development.

- Experience hiring, mentoring, and developing senior engineering talent.

- Track record of representing engineering functions to senior business stakeholders.

- Hands-on experience with Openclaw/Hermes agents.

Preferred Qualification
If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus

- Prior leadership experience at an AI-native company (Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, or similar) — Head of Forward Deployed Engineering, Director of Solutions, or equivalent.

- Experience in regulated industries (pharma, healthcare, financial services).

- Experience setting AI engineering standards at organizational scale.

- Clinical development experience.

About the job Build the software that validates Graphcore’s machine learning stack, from frameworks to AI accelerator hardware. You’ll design production-quality test infrastructure that engineers can extend, maintain and rely on as Graphcore’s ML software grows. Your work will help teams deliver reliable products, with clear evidence of numerical accuracy and performance across the stack. You’ll architect scalable test frameworks and build CI/CD pipelines that run across simulators, emulators and physical hardware. You’ll create representative ML workloads, analyse their execution and turn the results into practical improvements to testing and tooling. This role gives you scope to shape software architecture and developer experience, not just add tests to existing systems. You’ll deepen your understanding of the AI compute stack while solving engineering problems that connect software design with hardware behaviour. The team and culture Graphcore’s ML QA engineers build automation, work with industry-standard frameworks and models, and contribute to upstream open-source projects. You’ll work across software teams, using code and design reviews to strengthen quality, security and maintainability. You’ll use workload results to challenge assumptions and guide technical decisions about how Graphcore tests its ML stack. You’ll own improvements, act quickly on testing gaps and mentor junior engineers to raise the team’s technical standards. What we’re looking for Strong Python skills, demonstrated through designing, developing and maintaining production-quality software. Software design and architecture skills for large, complex codebases, with a focus on testability and long-term maintainability. Experience building CI/CD pipelines and automated testing systems in Linux environments. Familiarity with C or C++, including the ability to read, debug and reason about low-level code. The ability to mentor junior engineers and influence engineering practices through constructive feedback. A self-directed approach to solving complex problems, identifying gaps and driving improvements. While we have outlined a set of requirements, we value transferable skills and diverse experiences. We also welcome engineers returning to the profession after a career break, including through returnship routes. Who They Are A major UK bank with board-level backing for AI. This isn't a side project. They're building a small, high-impact AI Centre of Excellence from the ground up - and they need a technical leader who can shape it.

Why This Role Is Special
- Greenfield opportunity: Early in the AI journey, with governance frameworks, lifecycles and controls still being built. You'll put your stamp on how this is set up.

- Board-level backing: AI has strong top-down support. You'll help explain solutions and tooling to senior leaders.

- Truly hybrid role: Not pure engineering, not pure strategy. A genuine player-coach blend of technical leadership and hands-on delivery.

- Incredible benefits: 10% matched pension, up to 11% bonus, private medical (family cover), 30 days holiday plus bank holidays, and life assurance.

- Grown-up working culture: Outcomes matter more than presenteeism. This role is fully remote.

What You'll Own Technical Leadership & Delivery

- Lead design and delivery of AI solutions from concept through to production, working with a primary delivery partner and other partners, contractors and academic institutions.

- Be accountable for delivery outcomes, ensuring solutions are secure, scalable, compliant and aligned to Responsible AI principles.

- Shape technical direction, standards and best practice for AI engineering across the Group.

- Work with architecture, data, technology and business teams to identify and prioritise AI opportunities.

- Define the right build, buy and partner approach for AI solutions and services.

- Provide technical leadership across cloud-based AI platforms (Azure strategic, migrating from AWS), services and integrations.

- Support the growth of AI capability and adoption across the organisation.

Hands-On Engineering

- Get hands-on with code when needed, helping to build and deploy AI, Machine Learning and Generative AI solutions in production environments.

- Work with modern AI frameworks, LLMs, RAG, prompt engineering and vector databases.

- Ensure robust MLOps practices, APIs, data pipelines and modern software engineering disciplines are in place.

Strategic & Stakeholder Engagement

- Act as a thought leader, willing to challenge the business and drive new ways of working.

- Communicate clearly and confidently to senior leaders and board level, translating complex technical concepts into business language.

- Be a resilient change agent, pushing against colleagues who have done things the same way for years.

- Help establish engineering standards, frameworks and practices that enable AI solutions to be deployed securely, responsibly and at scale.

Must-Have
- Proven Production Experience: You have “lived it, breathed it.” Real commercial, production experience building and deploying AI/ML/GenAI solutions. Not just POC work or an academic pathway.

- Hybrid Technical & Strategic Skills: Deeply technical but able to present confidently to a board.

- Strong Engineering Foundation: Excellent Python and SQL skills. Terraform and CI/CD are must-haves.

- Regulated Environment Experience: You've worked in a corporate or regulated environment (financial services, public sector, insurance, etc.) and understand corporate governance.

- Consultancy Background (Preferred): Experience in consultancy is a strong fit - client engagement, stakeholder presentation, and balancing technical work with strategic advice.

- Thought Leadership & Resilience: Willing to challenge the status quo and drive new ways of working, even when faced with resistance.

- UK Right to Work: No sponsorship available.

Nice-to-Have
- Experience with Microsoft Azure, including Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Services, Azure Machine Learning and Azure Data Platform technologies.

- Knowledge of LLMs, RAG, prompt engineering, vector databases and modern AI frameworks.

- Experience with APIs, data pipelines, MLOps practices and modern software engineering disciplines.

- Experience managing partner-led delivery and a mix of onshore/offshore teams.

- Microsoft certifications (e.g., Azure AI Engineer, Azure Data Scientist).

The Process

Job title: AI Engineer

About us

Owlis is a UK IT managed services group, backed by private equity, that grows by bringing established regional IT providers together on one platform. Each business keeps its own name and its local relationships. Behind it sits one set of systems, one set of policies, and a group with the depth to support it properly. Together, we look after small and medium-sized businesses across the UK with managed IT, cybersecurity, and AI and transformation services.

About the role

When a client decides to use AI, someone has to build it, connect it to their systems and make it safe. This role works directly with clients, often on site, to build and deploy AI assistants, agents and automations on their data, then hands them over in a state our service desks can support.

Core systems

- Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI Search

- Copilot Studio and Power Platform

- Python and/or C#, Git, Azure DevOps or GitHub

- Microsoft Graph and client system APIs

- HaloPSA for project time, tasks and handover to support

What you will be doing

Build and deploy

- Design, build and deploy LLM applications for clients: assistants, retrieval over documents, agents and AI-assisted workflows

- Integrate with client systems through APIs, with scoped permissions

- Choose models and services to fit the client’s needs and budget, with the Head of AI

- Use version control, testing and deployment pipelines for everything we ship

Forward deployed with clients

- Work on site or remotely alongside client staff to understand the work and test with real users

- Explain what was built, how to use it and its limits in plain English

- Gather feedback after go-live and improve the build

Quality, security and support

- Build evaluation sets and monitoring for accuracy, cost and usage

- Apply least privilege, secrets management and client data handling rules

- Write handover documentation and runbooks for our service desks

- Record AI systems in our register with owners and risk ratings

Reuse and internal work

- Contribute connectors, templates and prompt and evaluation sets to a shared library

- Build internal AI tools for our own group companies

- Log time and tasks in HaloPSA

Outcomes and KPIs

- In the first 90 days: several client builds running, with reusable components (connectors, prompt and evaluation sets) in our shared library.

- By 6 months: 10 or more repeatable propositions delivered and rolled out to clients, each with standard scope, testing and handover.

- By 12 months: revenue targets met on the first 10 propositions, with more in flight.

Competencies

- Clear evidence of building and shipping LLM applications to real users, with integrations and testing described

- Explains retrieval or tool design, prompt and model choices, cost control and failure handling from first-hand work, and is honest about mistakes

- Builds integrations and automations with error handling, logging, least privilege and scoped service accounts, and uses vendor features before custom code

- Listens to clients and gets examples, explains plainly what the tool can and can’t do, and agrees a fix and a follow-up

- Designs a clear architecture (sources, indexing, permissions-aware retrieval, model, interface), talks through trade-offs and adapts when requirements change

- Uses security-trimmed retrieval, a tested evaluation set with agreed accuracy, and monitoring with a feedback loop, keeping data in the client’s tenant where possible

- Owns mistakes and fixes them, follows through and manages expectations when things slip

Essential skills and experience

- Has built and shipped applications using large language models, such as assistants, retrieval over documents (RAG) or agents

- Writes production-quality code in Python or C#, with version control and testing

- Has integrated AI or applications with business systems through APIs, for example Microsoft Graph, a CRM or a ticketing tool

- Builds with security and data protection in mind: least privilege, secrets handling and safe use of client data

- Can work directly with client users to understand a problem and explain what was built

Desirable skills and experience

- Experience with Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Search or Copilot Studio

- Has set up evaluation for AI outputs (test sets, accuracy measures, monitoring)

- Power Platform, Logic Apps or another workflow and integration tool

- Experience in an IT managed services provider or a client-facing engineering role

- Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102) or similar certification

- Infrastructure as code or CI/CD pipelines in Azure

Development

We expect the role to grow into a senior or lead AI engineer as the practice scales. Certification (for example AI-102) is supported where it fits the work.

Our recruitment process

Our process usually has four stages:

- A short pre-screening call with our HR / Recruitment team.

- A competency interview with the Head of AI / Operations Director

- A live system design exercise with a client scenario and a technical assessment

- A short final call with an Owlis Group executive, after which we aim to make an offer.

Any offer is conditional on two satisfactory professional references from employers named on your CV (with a work email address for each), proof of your right to work in the UK and a basic DBS check, because the role has privileged access to client systems and data. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship.

Job Description

Turn complexity into clarity.
At AJ Bell, we believe investing should feel good. Making that possible means continually understanding our customers, our business and the opportunities to improve how we work.
As a Senior Data Scientist, you'll turn complex and often loosely defined business questions into clear, actionable insight. You'll use Python, SQL, statistical methods and appropriate machine-learning techniques to understand what's happening, why it's happening and what could happen next.
You'll combine analytical rigour with commercial judgement and strong stakeholder engagement, making sure analysis doesn't stop at an interesting finding. Your work will help people make better decisions, understand opportunities and risks, and take practical action.
This is a role for someone who enjoys creating clarity from ambiguity. You'll work closely with senior stakeholders to understand the question behind the question, explore the data, develop robust analysis and communicate the "so what?" in a way that people can use.
What we're looking for

We're looking for someone who's curious, commercially minded and highly analytical. You'll be equally comfortable working in Python and SQL, discussing an uncertain question with a senior stakeholder and stepping back to explain the "so what?" in clear, straightforward language.
Most importantly, you'll be someone who enjoys turning ambiguity into clarity and analysis into decisions.
Essential

- Significant experience as a Data Analyst, Senior Data Analyst, Data Scientist, Insight Analyst or equivalent analytical professional.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to create clarity from ambiguous business questions.
- Advanced Python skills for data analysis and modelling, together with strong SQL capability.
- Practical experience applying statistical and data-science techniques to business problems, including several of forecasting, regression, classification, segmentation and propensity modelling.
- Sound understanding of statistical concepts, model evaluation, uncertainty, bias and the limitations of analytical approaches.
- Experience working with large or complex datasets and performing data discovery, validation and exploratory analysis.
- Excellent requirements-gathering, stakeholder-management and project-planning skills.
- Excellent written communication, with experience producing analytical papers or recommendations for senior audiences.
- Ability to translate complex analysis into concise conclusions, commercial implications and practical actions.
- Ability to iterate quickly, prioritise effectively and provide useful initial answers without waiting for perfectly defined requirements.
Desirable

- Experience with time-series techniques such as ARIMA, exponential smoothing or related forecasting methods.
- Experience developing customer churn, lifetime value, propensity, anomaly-detection or segmentation models.
- Experience analysing financial, operational, customer or risk data.
- Experience using machine-learning techniques beyond traditional statistical analysis.
- Experience with Snowflake or another cloud data platform, Streamlit, and Power BI
- Experience in financial services or another regulated, data-rich environment.

Having visibility of the entire pipeline from novel accelerator hardware to state-of-the-art AI applications, and the software stack in-between, you will play a critical role in identifying opportunities to innovate and differentiate Graphcore’s technology.

Furthermore, you’ll work closely with researchers in a rapidly-evolving field, where even the most senior engineers are constantly learning and adapting to exciting new challenges.

We seek engineers with strong technical foundations who are curious and eager to understand and advance AI model implementation, at scale.

We currently have multiple opportunities available in the team at Senior, Staff and Principal level and offer flexibility through a hybrid working model, from any of our UK offices.

If you're excited about advancing the next generation of AI models on cutting-edge hardware, we’d love to hear from you!

The team and culture

The Applied AI team’s role is to be proxies for our customers, we need to understand the latest AI models, applications, and software, as well as our own hardware and software stack, to ensure that Graphcore’s technology works seamlessly with the AI ecosystem and at scale.

Our work spans from low-level kernel development and optimisation for novel hardware through to implementing and scaling research-level algorithms for the latest AI models.

We collaborate with the Research team to develop and publish novel ideas in domains such as efficient compute, model scaling and distributed training and inference of AI models for multiple modalities and applications.

Responsibilities

- Implement and train state-of-the-art machine learning models and optimise for performance, accuracy and scalability across systems comprising 1000s of accelerators.

- Benchmark and profile ML models to identify performance bottlenecks.

- Develop deep understanding across the software stack in order to optimise kernel implementations.

- Test and evaluate new internal software releases, provide feedback to software engineering teams, make necessary code fixes, and conduct code reviews.

- Design and conduct experiments on novel AI methods and evaluate results.

- Collaborate with Research, Software, and Product teams to define, build, and test Graphcore’s next generation of AI hardware.

- Engage with AI community and keep in touch with the latest developments in AI.

What we’re looking for

Essential:

- Bachelor/Master's/PhD or equivalent experience in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Maths, Data Science, or related field.

- Proficiency in deep learning frameworks like PyTorch/JAX.

- Strong Python or C++ software development skills.

- Expertise in hardware-accelerated deep learning from model training to optimisation and evaluation.

- Capable of designing, executing and reporting from ML experiments.

- Well-developed understanding of performance bottlenecks and how to overcome them.

- Ability to move quickly in a fast-moving field.

Position Overview
As a Senior AI Application Engineer in the Model Enablement team (Application Software), you will own LLM and VLM support on Metis and Europa AIPUs, from studying new models to shipping them in the Voyager SDK.
The role combines LLM/VLM knowledge with solid software engineering. Our team uses AI coding agents in daily work, and you will use them to build, test and verify your own work.
We also welcome experienced field application engineers, technical leads and engineering managers who want to return to hands-on engineering. Experience in planning, delegating and reviewing work transfers well to working with AI agents.

Key responsibilities:

- LLM/VLM study: Study new LLM and VLM families and architectures (for example mixture-of-experts, small VLMs, new attention and decoding schemes). Prototype and profile them on Metis and Europa, and decide how they should run on our hardware.

- Productization: Turn your results and our ML research group's results into supported Voyager SDK features, with stable APIs, tests, documentation and release gates.

- Model-side contracts: For each LLM/VLM building block, own the PyTorch reference with quantization baked in, the weight mapping, and one contract that lists every input, output, weight and persistent state (such as a paged KV cache), and hand that contract to the compiler team. The runtime and tests use the same definition.

- Pipeline integration: Bring LLM and VLM serving into the Voyager SDK pipeline builder: prefill and decode, KV-cache management, streaming text output and multimodal inputs.

- Quality: With the regression and quantization owners, measure accuracy against the floating-point reference, and close or explain each gap.

- LLM/VLM bring-up platform: Extend the model enablement platform for LLM and VLM bring-up: environments with access to the compiler, runtime and real hardware (for example through MCP tools), closed-loop runs that apply a change, measure accuracy and speed against the reference and repeat, and evaluations that score each run.

- GenAI direction: Recommend what the Voyager SDK needs for GenAI, agents and speech on edge devices, and which model zoo demos show it best.

Qualifications:
Essential

- 5+ years of software engineering experience, with at least 2 years on ML inference, ML systems or ML tooling.

- Solid understanding of transformer inference: attention variants, KV caching, prefill versus decode, sampling, tokenization, and how a VLM joins a vision encoder to a language model.

- Working knowledge of LLM quantization (weight-only and weight-activation schemes, calibration, outlier handling), and the ability to tell a quantization loss from an implementation bug.

- Strong Python and PyTorch, and experience shipping production-quality software.

- Daily use of AI coding agents on real codebases, with good judgment about when to verify or reject their output.

- Ability to turn research code and hardware constraints into a practical design.

Preferred

- Experience with inference engines or serving stacks (for example llama.cpp, vLLM, ONNX Runtime GenAI, ExecuTorch).

- Experience with kernel development or a tensor compiler (for example Triton, TVM or MLIR), or with profiling models on accelerator hardware.

- Experience with speech (ASR, TTS) or agentic applications on embedded devices.

- Experience building evaluation or testing harnesses for ML systems or AI agents, or tool-calling agents (for example MCP servers).

Senior, Forward Deployed Engineer (Physical AI & Self-Driving Labs)

About GSK Enterprise AI
Enterprise AI is GSK’s centre of gravity for applied artificial intelligence. We pair forward deployed engineers and full-stack engineers with scientific, clinical, and business teams to build AI products that get used — not pilots that get archived. We work fast, ship in production, and measure ourselves on outcomes that matter to patients.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team — we welcome candidates from all backgrounds and underrepresented groups in technology, science, and pharma.

Position Summary
GSK’s Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the engineer GSK sends in to find out whether an AI idea will work — embedded with business unit (BU) teams, proving ideas through proofs of concept (PoCs), proofs of value (PoVs), and minimum viable products (MVPs) at a days-to-weeks cadence, then handing the proven solution off to the Sr. Solutions Engineer for scale-up. The pattern is proven by AI-native companies — Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI — and this role brings that model to GSK.

This specific role sites in the Chemical Manufacturing & Control (CMC) area. This is the GSK function that turns a validated molecule into a reliably manufactured, quality-assured medicine; its mission is to get safe, effective, consistently manufactured medicines to patients, faster. Its current mission is to double New Product Introductions (NPIs).

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be embedded in a team shaping how AI transforms GSK’s process development around the world. Most prototyping work is AI-augmented: AI coding assistants and multi-agent workflows handle the bulk of routine coding, freeing the FDE to focus on framing, judgement, and validation. The role works directly inside the customer’s business and emerges with working software and a defensible value hypothesis, not slideware. The FDE does not carry use cases through to long-term operations and partner with the Sr. Solutions Engineer is part of the role.

This role will build Physical AI capabilities to create self-driving labs and simulated tech transfers. You will work on orchestration of the physical space from the digital space. You will simulate the functioning of labs and a transfer to a line via virtual commissioning and Omniverse representations. This will support the ambitions of higher throughput and one-click deployment of a line. You will work hand in hand with the automation business and tech teams across R&D and manufacturing. You bring deep, hands-on AI/engineering expertise in Physical AI and the judgement to turn ambiguous technical problems into shipped, production-grade systems, while mentoring the engineers around you.

Key Responsibilities
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

PoC / PoV / MVP Delivery

- Take ownership of high-priority BU use cases from problem framing through to a working prototype, at days-to-weeks cadence, and form a defensible view on whether each should progress.
- Ship first production versions directly for use cases where the path is clear — before the Sr. Solutions Engineer takes them forward to scale.

AI-Native Engineering

- Operate AI agent workflows (planning, coding, testing, review, documentation) for autonomous prototype delivery — selecting the right level of automation for each engagement.
- Use AI coding assistants as the default mode of building; provide judgement, course correction, and validation.

Customer Embedding & Handoff

- Embed with BU teams — attend standups, understand the domain, prototype against real data and real workflows.
- Package proven use cases cleanly for the Sr. Solutions Engineer — working code, architecture rationale, open risks, and scaling concerns.

Governance, Standards & Coaching

- Begin Code Orange, Responsible AI, and Accountability Report conversations during prototyping — so the productionisation team does not inherit governance debt.
- Contribute reusable agents, prompt templates, and reference architectures to the organisation’s pattern library after each engagement.
- Form and defend kill/continue recommendations at the end of each engagement — presenting clearly to BU and Enterprise AI leadership.
- Coach BU engineers on AI-augmented ways of working while embedded, building BU capability alongside delivery outcomes.

Why You?
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals:

- Strong experience of full-stack or AI/ML engineering experience, including production deployments.

- Strong proficiency in Python and at least one of TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, or similar.

- Hands-on experience with GenAI patterns: agents, multi-agent orchestration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), prompt engineering, and evaluation.

- Strong experience in the physical space: labs, manufacturing control, edge deployment of models, predictive and anomaly detection modeling, closed-loop control.

- Strong experience in lab automation and self-driving lab workflows: robotics, instrument integration, and digital-to-physical orchestration that is aligned with the business platform and workflow (scheduling, execution and data capture).

- Strong experience in simulation of manufacturing lines and lab operations on physics-based or 3D simulation platforms such as NVIDIA Omniverse and Isaac Sim, applied to tech transfer, and with the NVIDIA physical AI and agentic model stack (Nemotron, etc.).

- Daily use of AI coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Databricks AI Assistant) as the primary mode of development.

Preferred Experience

- Prior experience as a Forward Deployed Engineer at an AI-native company (Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, or similar), or as a Customer Engineer / Solutions Architect at a hyperscaler.
- Experience in regulated industries (pharma, healthcare, financial services) and familiarity with good practice regulations (GxP), General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX).
- Experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems, Lab Execution Systems, etc.
- Experience extending lab automation into quality labs and manufacturing lines, working with automation, business and tech teams.
- Strong experience in computer vision systems, embedded systems and edge AI.
- Track record of contributing reusable engineering patterns back to a broader team.

Education

- Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Master’s degree in Computer Science or related field is advantageous

About GSK Enterprise AI
Enterprise AI is GSK’s centre of gravity for applied artificial intelligence. We pair forward deployed engineers and full-stack engineers with scientific, clinical, and business teams to build AI products that get used — not pilots that get archived. We work fast, ship in production, and measure ourselves on outcomes that matter to patients.

GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive team — we welcome candidates from all backgrounds and underrepresented groups in technology, science, and pharma.

Position Summary
GSK’s Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the engineer GSK sends in to find out whether an AI idea will work — embedded with business unit (BU) teams, proving ideas through proofs of concept (PoCs), proofs of value (PoVs), and minimum viable products (MVPs) at a days-to-weeks cadence, then handing the proven solution off to the Sr. Solutions Engineer for scale-up. The pattern is proven by AI-native companies — Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI — and this role brings that model to GSK.

This specific role sites in the Chemical Manufacturing & Control (CMC) area. This is the GSK function that turns a validated molecule into a reliably manufactured, quality-assured medicine; its mission is to get safe, effective, consistently manufactured medicines to patients, faster. Its current mission is to double New Product Introductions (NPIs).

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be embedded in a team shaping how AI transforms GSK’s process development around the world. Most prototyping work is AI-augmented: AI coding assistants and multi-agent workflows handle the bulk of routine coding, freeing the FDE to focus on framing, judgement, and validation. The role works directly inside the customer’s business and emerges with working software and a defensible value hypothesis, not slideware. The FDE does not carry use cases through to long-term operations and partner with the Sr. Solutions Engineer is part of the role.

This role will build agentic automation across the AI-native redesign of our process development in R&D. You will turn manual, repetitive workflows into agentic workflows covering data capture, analysis and experimental planning. You will work hand in hand with the data analytics team in process science and partner with the R&D Tech teams. You will foster decision making embedded inside the teams instead of wasting time in wider forums, to reduce time to impact. You bring deep, hands-on AI/engineering expertise and the judgement to turn ambiguous technical problems into shipped, production-grade systems, while mentoring the engineers around you.

Key Responsibilities
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:
PoC / PoV / MVP Delivery

- Take ownership of high-priority BU use cases from problem framing through to a working prototype, at days-to-weeks cadence, and form a defensible view on whether each should progress.
- Ship first production versions directly for use cases where the path is clear — before the Sr. Solutions Engineer takes them forward to scale.

AI-Native Engineering

- Operate AI agent workflows (planning, coding, testing, review, documentation) for autonomous prototype delivery — selecting the right level of automation for each engagement.
- Use AI coding assistants as the default mode of building; provide judgement, course correction, and validation.

Customer Embedding & Handoff

- Embed with BU teams — attend standups, understand the domain, prototype against real data and real workflows.
- Package proven use cases cleanly for the Sr. Solutions Engineer — working code, architecture rationale, open risks, and scaling concerns.

Governance, Standards & Coaching

- Begin Code Orange, Responsible AI, and Accountability Report conversations during prototyping — so the productionisation team does not inherit governance debt.
- Contribute reusable agents, prompt templates, and reference architectures to the organisation’s pattern library after each engagement.
- Form and defend kill/continue recommendations at the end of each engagement — presenting clearly to BU and Enterprise AI leadership.
- Coach BU engineers on AI-augmented ways of working while embedded, building BU capability alongside delivery outcomes.

ABOUT FRACTILE

Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.

The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems.

Find out why AI recommends one brand over another. Turn our AI search data into the GEO playbook, the recommendation engine and the models that tell customers what to do next.
About Obsero
Obsero is one of the UK's leading AI search startups. We track how brands are cited and recommended across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Mode and Claude, so marketing teams can see where they stand in AI answers and what to do about it.
The problem
Every day our platform runs thousands of prompts across the major AI platforms and records what comes back: which brands get mentioned, which sources get cited, how they are described and how that changes over time. It is now one of the richest datasets on AI search anywhere. Today the platform tells customers where they stand. The question every marketer actually wants answered is why an LLM recommends one brand over another, and what they should do about it. Your job is to answer it, and to take the platform from insight to action.
Why join now

- We've just raised $1.2m, led by SFC Capital, to build specialist AI agents trained on the GEO playbook from a year of client work
- In our first year we captured and analysed over 10 million AI answers, and that number is growing fast
- You'll be the first data scientist, so you'll set how we turn that data into insight
- Meaningful equity, alongside a salary of £80,000 to £100,000
The role
This is a lead role reporting to a founder. You will own the problem end to end, from a clean, trusted dataset through to models running in the product. Our lead data engineer owns how the data is captured, cleaned and stored, so your time goes on what it means rather than on fixing it.
What you'll own

- The GEO playbook: using our historic prompt data to understand what drives LLMs to recommend one brand over another, separating the factors that genuinely move visibility from the ones that only look like they do
- The recommendation engine: productising Obsero's GEO recommendation engine in the platform, and measuring whether recommendations work so results feed back into the engine
- Predictive models: predicting the likely impact of different actions for each customer, so they know what to do first
- New insight: exploring new ways to analyse the data, prototyping quickly and turning the best ideas into features
This is not a reporting or dashboarding role. We want someone who asks better questions of the data than we do, and builds the models and products that answer them.
What you'll need

- Several years of hands-on data science, with a track record of taking models from analysis into production
- Strong Python and SQL, comfortable building the analysis and feature pipelines your models need
- Statistical modelling, causal inference or experimentation, and the judgement to tell correlation from cause in messy, real-world data
- Experience with recommendation systems, ranking or predictive modelling
- Hands-on with LLMs and NLP, and properly curious about how AI platforms decide what to recommend
- The ability to explain complex findings clearly to marketers, consultants and founders
- Product-minded, focused on what will change a customer's results
- Comfortable owning a problem end to end in a small team
Nice to have

- An understanding of SEO or GEO
You'll need to be based in the UK with the right to work here.
What success looks like

- A GEO playbook grounded in evidence that our consultants and customers use
- A recommendation engine live in the platform, with customers acting on what it tells them
- Measurable improvement in customer visibility from the actions it prioritises
- Insight that sets Obsero apart from every other AI search tool
How we hire
Intro call with the Chief Product Officer, a technical conversation with our lead engineer, a presentation and then meeting the CEO.

Apply through the link on this ad. Tell us briefly about a model you took from idea to production, and what difference it made.

Role: Senior AI Impact & Applied Innovation Specialist
Location: Cambridge UK
Salary: Competitive + Excellent Benefits

Are you ready to translate AstraZeneca's frontier AI capabilities into concrete impact for the organisation? The Applied AI Research team, part of the AI Science Innovation (AISI) group within Enterprise AI (EAI), sits at the intersection of frontier AI research and oncology R&D, with a mission to ensure that advances in foundation models, agentic systems, and biological AI find their way to the problems where they will have the greatest impact on how we discover and develop medicines.

As Senior AI Impact & Applied Innovation Specialist , Applied AI Research, you will be involved in both sides of that translation: identifying where frontier AI can address fundamental drug discovery questions for AstraZeneca, and orchestrating focused cross-departmental projects to answer them. You will maintain a structured view of AZ's highest-value AI science problems – mapping which questions most need answers, which frameworks are now mature enough to address them, and where AZ's unique data, biology, and portfolio create irreplaceable scientific advantage. You will also act as the scientific lead and orchestrator for delivering against those problems, assembling the right combination of expertise and resources and holding the scientific hypothesis through to a result that changes a decision.

This is a role for someone familiar with key questions across the drug discovery pipeline, who can attend a frontier AI seminar and immediately see which ideas are applicable to areas from target identification to trial design, and who has the scientific conviction to advocate for a particular problem in the face of competing priorities.

If you thrive at the intersection of machine learning and translational oncology and want to leave a direct mark on the scientific questions that shape AstraZeneca's pipeline, this role is for you.

Typical Accountabilities

AI Landscape & Opportunity Mapping:

- Maintain an interactive framework providing a structured, dynamic inventory of AZ's internal and external AI capabilities, including frontier models and platforms.

- Identify high-priority scientific questions—such as those in target discovery, combination therapy, tumor mapping, and trial design—where frontier AI can deliver significant value. Distinguish opportunities unique to AstraZeneca from those addressable with generic tools or public data.

Scientific Evaluation Standards:

- Apply scientific expertise and evaluation standards to AI-driven frameworks designed to maintain a live, structured record of R&D goals and decision-making.

- Design and apply evaluation approaches for generative and agentic systems, including harnesses, benchmarks, trajectory-level metrics and validated LLM-as-judge methods, and run structured red-teaming (adversarial testing, failure-mode taxonomies, pre-release and continuous monitoring).

- Advise on and test where AI agents can responsibly automate steps in scientific, clinical and operational research processes, defining oversight points, acceptance criteria and comparison with the manual baseline.

Forward-Deployed Embedding & Delivery:

- Translate scientific hypotheses into well-specified, time-bounded projects with pre-defined success criteria, with a clear path to integration and deployment; orchestrate the delivery of these projects

- Establish frameworks for quantifying impacts of AI projects and measuring impact for the business and implement these for active cross-functional projects.

Stakeholder Communication & Leadership:

- Communicate AI science priorities, programmed status, and strategic recommendations to senior stakeholders across EAI, Oncology R&D and Biopharma R&D; act as the scientific bridge between AISI strategy and execution-layer teams, ensuring that frontier insight translates into actionable work and that delivery blockers are visible to leadership.

Essential Requirements:

- Advanced degree (PhD preferred; Master's with substantial relevant experience considered) in a quantitative biological or computational discipline: computational biology, bioinformatics, machine learning, statistics, or a closely related field.

- Demonstrated experience applying AI/ML methods to clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, or other biomedical data in a drug development or translational research context.

- Strong scientific literacy across the oncology drug development pipeline, from target identification and preclinical biology through biomarker development, clinical trial design, and Phase 1/2 decision-making.

- Familiarity with the current landscape of AI in drug development, including foundation models for biological and clinical data, perturbation prediction, digital pathology, and agentic research systems.

- Demonstrated ability to frame rigorous scientific or clinical questions and translate them into tractable AI problems with well-specified success criteria.

- Experience evaluating the quality of AI models in a scientific or clinical context, including understanding of validation standards, confounding, shortcut learning, and the distinction between prognostic and predictive signals.

- Track record of working effectively across multidisciplinary teams, including both technical AI/ML specialists and experimental or clinical scientists.
- Excellent written and oral scientific communication, including the ability to present technical material to non-technical senior audiences and to distil complex landscapes into actionable recommendations.
- Comfort with ambiguity and a bias for action; able to make well-reasoned prioritization decisions under uncertainty and to advocate for them.

Desirable Requirements:

- Direct experience with generative AI and agentic systems applied to life sciences, particularly for clinical insights.
- Direct experience with multimodal foundation models, particularly for computational pathology, for response prediction, subtyping and other common research tasks.

- Direct experience with multimodal data integration, for example combining clinical, genomic, transcriptomic, imaging, and/or pathology data.

- Familiarity with CRISPR functional genomics, perturbation prediction, or virtual cell approaches and their application to target discovery or combination prioritization.

- Familiarity with AI benchmarking methodologies and the challenges of evaluating foundation models on clinically meaningful tasks.

- Experience with AI prioritization or portfolio management methodologies – including problem identification, value assessment, and structured decision frameworks.
- A record of scientific contribution (e.g., peer-reviewed publications), ideally including AI/ML or clinical AI venues, that establishes credibility with technical, clinical, and scientific audiences

THE ROLE

We're looking for an exceptional Forward Deployed Software Engineer (FDSE) to join our engineering team. This is an engineering-first role: FDSEs are the technical owners who take the Encord platform into our most strategic and advanced customer environments, working directly with users and their engineering teams to understand complex problems, make system design decisions, and build production software that solves them.

As an early member of the Forward Deployed team, you'll have an outsized impact on shaping a critical engineering function at Encord. You'll work hands-on across the stack, from APIs and data workflows to backend services and product surfaces, while owning technical problems end to end. You'll make architecture decisions under real production constraints, debug complex integrations and workflows, and build solutions that can scale beyond a single customer or use case. You'll operate autonomously, defining the right technical approach with limited guidance, building trusted relationships with users, and feeding what you learn directly back into the product and engineering roadmap.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Design and build production software for complex data, ML, and application environments

- Own system design decisions for deployments, balancing correctness, scalability, performance, and speed

- Work directly with customers and their engineering teams to understand ambiguous problems and define the right technical solution

- Build across the stack, from APIs and data workflows to backend systems and product-facing functionality

- Own deployments from technical scoping through implementation, rollout, and iteration

- Turn recurring customer problems into reusable tooling and product capabilities

- Debug complex production issues across reliability, performance, and data flow

- Communicate technical decisions and trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders

- Operate with high autonomy and own problems end to end

- Feed deployment insights back into Product and Engineering, and help shape the FDSE function as the team grows

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- A strong software engineer. You have solid fundamentals and the technical depth to design and build complex production systems

- A first-principles problem solver. You dig into the underlying problem, challenge assumptions, and make sound technical and product trade-offs rather than defaulting to the obvious solution

- A strong communicator and stakeholder partner. You can build trust, navigate competing priorities, and explain complex decisions clearly

- An autonomous builder. You operate with limited guidance, create structure from ambiguity, and drive problems through to production

- A versatile product engineer. You’re comfortable working across the stack and moving between hands-on engineering, product thinking, and conversations with the people using what you build

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

- 4+ years of software engineering experience with strong CS fundamentals

- Experience building production software across the stack, from product-facing applications and APIs to backend services and data workflows

- Strong system design judgment and experience making architecture decisions for complex software

- Strong coding skills in a modern language; Python is a plus

- Evidence of owning technical problems end to end, from design through production

- Strong product judgment, technical communication, and stakeholder management

- Experience working directly with users, customers, or external engineering teams is a plus

- Bonus: experience in a high-growth startup, developer platform, or ML/data product environment

WHY ENCORD

- Competitive salary, commission, and meaningful equity in a high-growth startup

- Clear, accelerated growth opportunities as the company scales rapidly

- Strong in-person culture: 4 days/week

- Daily team lunches & dinners

- Annual learning & development budget

- US employees: 18 paid vacation days plus US public holidays

- UK employees: 25 paid vacation days plus UK public holidays

THE ROLE

We're looking for a Research Engineer to join Encord's ML team. You'll work on robotics, computer vision and multimodal research in data curation, annotation, evaluation and quality control, with successful work going into the core product.

We face a variety of interesting research problems across the full data life-cycle, including annotation, quality control, verification and curation. We are looking to strengthen our team to build upon and extend our market-leading platform. The kind of problems we solve are constantly evolving alongside the needs of our frontier customers, including many of the leading robotics and physical AI teams. Join us as we leverage our massive flow of proprietary data on our journey to develop generalised solutions applicable across diverse multi-modal tasks.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Form hypotheses, design experiments, and drive original research on open problems from leading robotics and AI customers

- Research and prototype agentic workflows which can handle multimodal inputs and diverse customer ontologies

- Advance our work on data curation and model evaluation

- Tackle egocentric video understanding, from captioning to deeper 3d understanding

- Build working prototypes to test ideas end to end, then partner with our ML systems and Product Engineering teammates to bring them into the platform

- Help shape our longer-term research direction and bring the most relevant ideas from the field back to the team

- Publish research papers and present your work at conferences and workshops

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

- A builder with a research mindset. You can take an open-ended problem, form a hypothesis and get to a working prototype without a detailed spec.

- A first-principles problem solver. You lean on strong fundamentals rather than surface-level familiarity with the latest trends.

- A big-picture thinker. You're excited by ambitious, longer-term problems and know how to break them into steps.

- A multiplier. You raise the level of the team around you by shaping research direction, mentoring others and turning findings into decisions.

EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS

- A PhD in computer vision, machine learning or a related field, or equivalent applied research experience

- A strong background in computer vision and multimodal ML, whether in traditional CV, modern VLMs and embedding models, or both

- Clear evidence of independent research, such as publications, a thesis, open-source work or applied research where you owned the original contribution

- Solid mathematical foundations in statistics, probability and linear algebra

- Strong Python and PyTorch skills, and experience running experiments end-to-end

- A genuine interest in data-centric AI: curation, evaluation and data quality

- Bonus: experience applying LLM-based agents to visual tasks, or working with video, 3D or other complex data types
